name: display-mode
plain: How the page is shown: browser tab, standalone, fullscreen, PWA.
meaning: Shows the app was installed as a PWA and whether the person runs it in a window. Useful for install analytics.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: display-mode
fields.range: browser, standalone, minimal-ui, fullscreen, window-controls-overlay, picture-in-picture

limits.headline: Can tell whether it is open in a browser tab, a home screen app or fullscreen
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads or the window changes.
can: Check which display mode it is running in
Hide install buttons when it is already an app
Change its layout to fit app or tab
cannot: See which other apps you have installed
Tell whether you also installed it on another device
Install itself without you choosing to

story.what_it_is: Tells a page whether it runs in a normal tab, as an installed app window, or full screen.

marketing.name: Progressive Web Apps
marketing.pitch: Google pitches installable web apps that open in their own window like a native app.

marketing.name: display-mode media feature
marketing.pitch: Documents how a page can detect if it runs in a browser tab or as an installed app.

story.for_you: You never see the check. But an app you installed from your browser may hide the address bar and show its own simple menu.
story.for_makers: Makers change the layout for installed mode, hide the install prompt, and measure how many people install. Installed users usually come back more often, so it is a key business signal.

use_cases.example: A to do app hides its 'Install' banner and shows a bottom tab bar once it runs as an installed app.
A social site counts how many daily users come from the installed version to see whether installs lift return visits.
A browser game offers fullscreen play and landscape layout when launched from the home screen.
A music or video site shows its own back button because the browser one is gone.
A store gives installed users a faster checkout and push notification offer.
A team tags installed sessions in analytics to compare them against tab visits.

legit_uses: Respect OS theme and accessibility needs
abuse: Infer disability or setting for fingerprinting
